name: Dusty rust
lede: Dusty rust renders Kaba-iro (蒲色), a traditional Japanese name meaning "cattail color", after the brown-orange flower spike of the cattail plant.

sections.title: Named for the cattail
sections.body:
Our color library gives the source as 蒲色 (Kaba-iro), "cattail color", from the traditional colors of Japan; 蒲 (kaba) is the cattail, a marsh plant whose dense, brown-orange flower spike this name points to [1]. No first-recorded date survives in our sources, so exactly when the name entered use is undocumented here [1].

The nearest named color in our graph is [[yellowish-sienna]], at a color distance (ΔE2000) of 2.8, a duller shade; [[rust]] itself sits 3.3 away and reads more vivid by comparison [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this rust in 312 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.3 percent, as photographed [3]. It peaks in the 1400s (7 of 73 paintings from that decade), more than three-and-a-half times the overall rate, with Filippo Lippi's paintings carrying it at over three times his peers' usage [3]. By country it is strongest in Nepali and Tibetan painting, each running about six and three times the archive average, and in Indian work more broadly [3]. The earliest dated match is a Buddhist votive card from the year 1000, a floor set by what survives and was photographed, not a first appearance [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings; the match is computed, not a pigment identification [3].
